notes: All 7 old-skill failures across evals 0-2 share ONE root cause: the v1.0 guide lacks the service/usecase layer split (services were DB-backed business logic wired straight into handlers). The new skill fixes exactly this.
Eval 0 (full scaffold) is the strongest discriminator: 100% vs 29% — old skill stopped at Repository/Service bundles with no internal/app/usecase.go.
Eval 3 (middlewares) is non-discriminating (100% both): that area of the spec did not change between v1.0 and v1.1.
Old-skill runs were NOT bad code — they produced clean, compiling services; they simply followed the outdated architecture. This confirms the skill (not general capability) drove the difference.
Timing/token metrics unavailable this iteration: subagent completion notifications did not report total_tokens/duration_ms, so time/token comparisons are 0.

Eval-improvement notes from graders: (1) 'handler actions are methods on *Handlers' is overbroad since Healthz/Metrics stay package-level functions; (2) eval-3 assertion 'both registered via e.Use()' contradicts the guide's own api.Use() group scoping for JWT; (3) no assertion checks that the generated slice compiles on its own.
Baseline agents hit the skill's 'ask which wiring pattern' step in non-interactive runs and defaulted sensibly to Private DI; the new skill could state that fallback explicitly.
